highlights.title: Why it matters that President Trump just dialed into a NASA news conference
highlights.summary: As is standard procedure for major NASA missions, the US space agency held a post-launch news conference on Sunday morning at Kennedy Space Center in Florida to provide information about how the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope was faring during its initial maneuvers.
body: What was not standard, however, is what happened in the middle of the news conference. A little less than half an hour in, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman looked down at his mobile phone, and then stood up and walked away from the dais where he had been seated behind a table along with other NASA officials. He briefly left the room.

Isaacman returned about a minute later, phone in hand, apologizing for interrupting NASA’s chief of science, Nicky Fox, as she was speaking about the mission. “The President of the United States of America would like to address and congratulate everyone on this mission,” Isaacman said, returning to his seat.

In an unusual moment, Trump then spoke through Isaacman’s phone to the assembled reporters and NASA officials. “I just want to thank everybody, and congratulate you. Boy, it looked beautiful on television,” Trump said of the Roman space telescope launch. “Jared is doing a fantastic job, you are doing a fantastic job, and I’m supplying you all that money.”

highlights.title: Musk’s faster path to more gas turbines comes with pollution problem
highlights.summary: Elon Musk says a secretive new SpaceX foundry will let him cast his own turbine blades and get gas power online 18 months faster than anyone else — but it's a bet on a fuel source that's already triggering lawsuits and health studies everywhere his (and others') turbines have gone in.
body: Elon Musk says he’s found a way to solve one of AI’s biggest bottlenecks by making a hard-to-manufacture turbine part himself.

“SpaceX and Tesla are each building 100GW/year of solar production capacity as fast as possible,” Musk wrote on X on Saturday, “but natural gas will still be needed to supplement and bootstrap solar for several years. The limiting factor for nat gas turbine production is casting the blades & vanes. By doing in-house casting at SpaceX, we can accelerate nat gas turbines coming online by up to 18 months, which is a profound game-changer.”

The “why” of all this goes back to one of the biggest challenges facing the AI industry right now. GPU shortages are still an issue — Nvidia’s newest Blackwell chips are still running lead times of several months, for example — but a second constraint has emerged alongside it, which is the physical power grid. The International Energy Agency projects global data center electricity use will roughly double by 2030, and gas turbine maker GE Vernova says it’s essentially sold out of production capacity through 2030 due largely to AI infrastructure demand.

highlights.title: Fernandes hat-trick helps Man Utd come from behind to beat Ipswich
highlights.summary: Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick as Manchester United came from behind to beat Ipswich 5-2 at Old Trafford and pick up their first win of the season.
body: It looked like being a difficult afternoon for Michael Carrick's team early on. Julio Enciso and Daizen Maeda both forced smart stops from Senne Lammens before Abdul Fatawu skinned Luke Shaw and fed Leif Davis to side-foot the opener high into the United net.

Old Trafford was edgy at that point, with United having lost to Hull on the opening weekend. But the game turned when Marcelino Nunez slipped over. Matheus Cunha robbed the Chilean midfielder and found Fernandes, who slammed the ball home with his left foot.

Bryan Mbeumo should have completed the turnaround early in the second half only to strike the bar from close range, but United did not have to wait long. Their second was not without controversy, however, as Harry Maguire escaped punishment for a handball.

Had his shot gone straight into the net then it would have been disallowed but because the attempt was diverted in by Jacob Greaves, it was allowed to stand. Moments later, United took the game away from Ipswich as Greaves' unfortunate afternoon continued.

highlights.title: Fable's Main Quest Will Take About 20 Hours to Beat
highlights.summary: Fable 's main quest will take around 20 hours to beat, Playground Games has confirmed. Associate game directors Will Kennedy and Craig Littler shared the estimated length for the 2027 fantasy RPG during a group Q&A attended by Polygon at gamescom 2026.
body: "We have around 15-20 hours of mainline quest gameplay, we have around 15-20 of side and open-world exploration content gameplay," Kennedy said.

As sprawling RPGs have continued to fill the space, that might come up a bit short for what some players were expecting. Open-world games like Elden Ring, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Assassin's Creed Valhalla have famously delivered massive worlds with main quests that could have players spending 50 hours or more just to complete the story. For Fable, that won't be the case, but longtime fans probably expected that.

Howlongtobeat has the original 2004 Fable 's main quest clocking in at about 12 and a half hours. Fable 2 isn't much longer at 13 hours, and Fable 3 inches just further past that at 13 and a half hours. If anything, next year's Fable reboot is already shaping up to be the longest in the series, and pushing its main campaign on much longer would have it launching with a story almost twice as long as the one in the original game.

highlights.title: ‘People should not feel guilty’: weekend lie-in may be good for you, experts say
highlights.summary: Previous advice stressed risks of sleeping in but about 90 minutes extra could prevent high blood pressure. For years, experts have stressed the risks of lie-ins, warning that catching up on missed sleep at the weekend can disrupt the body’s internal clock and trigger adverse health effects.
body: Now analysis has produced a heartening caveat to that advice: if you do not overdo it, weekend lie-ins may be good for you, with an ideal benchmark of 1hr 27min extra in bed to protect against high blood pressure.

Most experts still agree that setting a routine bedtime and wake-up time is key to maintaining good health. But a new study shows a modest amount of catch-up sleep – one to two hours extra – after a long week is associated with a lower prevalence of high blood pressure.
Globally, more than 1.3 billion people have hypertension. They face a much higher risk of heart attack, stroke, kidney disease and early death.

While other ways to avoid high blood pressure remain crucial – such as staying active, maintaining a healthy weight and eating well – the study suggests people should no longer feel guilty about getting up late at the weekend, experts said.

highlights.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to study dark matter and dark energy
highlights.summary: After funding struggles and a name change, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been successfully launched. It will now make a three-month, one-million-mile journey to its orbit at the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2) beyond the Moon.
body: From this vantage point, Roman will conduct an unprecedented survey of the universe. Its field of view is 100 times larger than Hubble’s and, according to NASA, it can survey the sky 1,000 times faster using its 300-megapixel infrared camera. Roman also has a Coronagraph system that can block and mask glare from stars, allowing it to directly image exoplanets, even smaller, older, and colder planets orbiting close to their stars.

Roman will also conduct detailed 3D scans to help map the distribution of dark matter and narrow down the potential candidates for its makeup. Using the same 3D scans and gravitational lensing measurements, Roman will attempt to map how dark energy shaped the evolution of the universe.

Nicky Fox, associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate at NASA, said in a press release that “Roman will be a discovery machine that will bring us closer than ever before to answering humanity’s most profound questions about our cosmic history.”

highlights.title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
highlights.summary: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites. It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.
body: Nearly every company that’s trying to deploy artificial intelligence runs into the same problem: it’s hard to integrate the tech into everyday operations. Industrial heavyweight Caterpillar has spent decades dealing with a version of that problem in the physical world, and now it’s using its experience to deploy AI.

Caterpillar’s push into the autonomous space started with mining, where labor shortages and hazardous conditions can make automation particularly useful. Today, it sells automated haul trucks, drilling, underground loaders, dozers, remote-controlled construction equipment, and more. It also offers a software command center, fleet management, and even remote terrain intelligence as part of its autonomous toolkit.

“Now we’re in this super exciting time where we can take all of that learning from mining and bring it into much more dynamic environments, jobsites, quarries, and construction sites,” the company’s CTO, Jaime Mineart, told TechCrunch on the sidelines of the Ai4 conference in Las Vegas earlier this month.

"I think the guys have shown great adaptability," Root said. "We've overcome some difficult situations when we were at 80-4 to get the total that we did.

highlights.title: The lost art of guilt-free relaxation on Sundays | Letters
highlights.summary: Readers respond to an article about le dimanche français, the French Sunday, being the secret to happiness. What Polly Hudson describes as le dimanche français is almost a description of the very British Sundays of my youth ( Is a French Sunday the secret to a healthier, happier life?, 23 August ).
body: We enjoyed a good book (not a heavy one), an afternoon film on TV, board games, cards, or a gentle stroll for the pleasure of it rather than as part of a keep-fit regime. And let us not forget time to peruse the Sunday newspapers. Children got bored and learned how to entertain themselves, a skill today’s hard-pressed parents underestimate as they struggle to ensure Sundays are packed with activities.

There were no home computers and shops were closed, as were cinemas, swimming pools, theme parks and even pubs in certain parts of the country. This was occasionally frustrating, but more usually an advantage, removing the temptation to feel like one ought to be doing something, thus enhancing a guilt-free mindset. It was wonderful.
Importantly, it was the same day of the week for everyone. That made a difference. The whole atmosphere was quieter.
So what changed? My impression is that the whole rhythm of the week changed with Sunday trading. I’m not sure a younger generation would even recognise the phrase. Oh, were it possible to go back.

highlights.title: Google Maps Now Shows ‘Lake America’ Instead of Lake Ontario
highlights.summary: After Donald Trump’s executive order demanding the name change, Google is the first major online maps provider to flip the switch.
body: Lake Ontario is no more on Google Maps in the US. Google changed the name of easternmost of the Great Lakes to “Lake America” late Saturday, days after President Donald Trump ordered its rebranding in official government databases.

Trump issued the executive order on Thursday as part of an ongoing feud over tariffs with Canada, whose capital province is called Ontario. It followed a similar order he issued in January 2025 to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America as part of a fight with the US trading partner to the south.

Google, Apple, Microsoft, and other maps providers adopted the Gulf of America naming as soon as the US Department of the Interior updated its records, which came a couple of weeks after Trump’s order. So it was no surprise that when those records —which are used to determine names on roadway signs and in government literature—reflected Lake America, digital maps from Google also quickly took on the new name.
points: After Donald Trump’s executive order demanding the name change, Google is the first major online maps provider to flip the switch.

highlights.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
highlights.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed suit against Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California seeking damages for "tens of thousands" copyrighted works.
body: The companies call it “one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history.”

This is just the latest high-profile suit against Anthropic, which recently settled a suit brought by the publishing industry for $1.5 billion. It’s also faced multiple lawsuits from Universal Music Group, Concord, and ABKCO, plus separate suits from BMG and Round Hill Music.

In addition to suing Anthropic as an entity, the complaint names Co-Founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann as individual defendants. The suit alleges that Mann used BitTorrent to download over five million pirated books, and that employees downloaded at least two million more from Pirate Library Mirror. It also claims that Anthropic scraped lyrics from sites like MusixMatch and LyricFind, which paid to license content from the labels.

highlights.title: The datacenter backlash is bringing the entire political spectrum together – against Big Tech billionaires
highlights.summary: The movement against datacenters is uniting Americans because they perfectly illustrate how a few individuals hold all the power to control decisions that impact our lives. Bryce Gustafson has been knocking on doors in Indiana for more than a decade.
body: Gustafson said he’s had similar conversations all across the state. If there’s one thing he sees uniting Hoosiers of all stripes – from rural areas such as Morgan county to suburbs such as Franklin Township to the historically African American neighborhood of Martindale-Brightwood in Indianapolis – it’s fury over these water-guzzling, air-polluting behemoths and the tech oligarchs imposing them.

Today, three-quarters of Americans oppose local datacenter development, a swing of more than 30 points in just a year. More than 500 counties and municipalities have passed datacenter bans or moratoria, while dozens of proposed projects have been killed outright. And the issue has come to define some of the highest-profile political races in the country. In the battle for US Senate in Ohio, populist Democrat Sherrod Brown has made Republican senator Jon Husted’s support of datacenters the centerpiece of his campaign, prompting warnings from the National Republican senatorial committee that “datacenters are the anchor hanging around Husted’s neck”.

highlights.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
highlights.summary: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists.
body: As AI infiltrates the electronic dance music scene, a callout culture is brewing.

For musicians — especially those creating art in technologically-focused spaces like electronic dance music — the increasingly complicated question of what is “real” and what isn’t feels particularly urgent and personal. Professional courtesy can make this only more complex; listeners can call out performers they suspect of using gen AI, but it’s something else for artists to raise concerns about their professional peers. There are some though, like 26-year-old EDM producer Max “H4RRIS” Harris, who are taking a stand against generative technology with videos calling out anyone they believe is trying to pass off AI slop as human-made art.

When I recently spoke with Harris, he told me that he sees AI-generated music as “a kind of decoy art form,” and he thinks that the people making it don’t really have anything meaningful to say with their creations. He feels that true art in any medium is “created by people that are trying to express feelings and messages,” and he believes that the only thing AI boosters are really interested in is making a quick profit.

highlights.title: 'Coyote Vs. ACME' Beat 'The Odyssey' And Ridley Scott At The Box Office This Weekend
highlights.summary: While Coyote vs. ACME didn't top the box office charts on its opening weekend, it beat out the likes of The Odyssey and a new movie from Ridley Scott. Considering the movie had to be promoted and released independently by Ketchup Entertainment after Warner Bros.
body: Deadline reports that Coyote vs. ACME grossed $15.4 million over the course of its first weekend. It has already grossed nearly double what the Looney Tunes film The Day the Earth Blew Up earned during its entire run. Although $15.4 million might seem like a modest opening weekend gross in a summer full of blockbusters, Deadline's reporting highlights that the flick only had a $10 million marketing budget, as Ketchup Entertainment had to handle the entire release itself.

Coyote vs. ACME was originally produced by Warner Bros., but the studio decided to shelve the film in 2023 and take a $30 million write-off on it. Ketchup Entertainment obtained the rights to release it and has done so on its own, making the fact that Coyote vs. ACME is coming to theaters and finding success at all very impressive.

The reviews for Coyote vs. ACME have been glowing too, with Polygon's Brian VanHooker writing, "As a lifelong Looney Tunes fan who has been very invested in this whole drama, it was entirely worth the wait."

highlights.title: Why Owner of ‘Heated Rivalry’ Cottage Did Some “Soul Searching” Before Agreeing to Season 2
highlights.summary: The now-famous cottage served as the emotional backdrop for a major turning point in the queer hockey romance show's first season, which starred Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie.
body: The owner of the cottage made famous in Heated Rivalry season one says he needed to do some “soul searching” before allowing production to return for season two.

During a recent interview with HGTV, Michael Kutryk revealed that he was contacted about filming for the highly anticipated second season, which got underway earlier this month. However, he said it wasn’t an immediate yes.

In season one of HBO Max and Crave’s breakout queer hockey romance, the cottage served as the emotional backdrop for a major turning point. When Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) invited his secret lover, Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie), to his private cottage for a two-week stay of uninterrupted alone time together, it led to them growing closer and ultimately confessing their love for each other. But the cottage also played a role in Ilya and Shane deciding to come out to the latter’s parents after Shane’s father accidentally caught them together at the home.

highlights.title: I have diarrhea. What should I do?
highlights.summary: The discussion about diarrhea has increased lately, especially with the rise of cyclosporiasis. Although unpleasant, it is manageable and can be treated at home. In the US, people are discussing diarrhea more than usual.
body: Some causes, such as cyclospora infection, benefit from antibiotic treatment. But most episodes of diarrhea go away by themselves and don’t require treatment apart from staying hydrated, says Benjamin Levy, a gastroenterologist at the University of Chicago.
Although it’s unpleasant, it’s usually manageable. Here’s how to know when to seek care, and how to take care of yourself at home.
The majority of diarrhea episodes go away by themselves after three or four days, says Levy.

However, if you have diarrhea that has lasted longer than a week or is accompanied by fever or other concerning symptoms, seek care. These include a fever of 101F or higher, blood or mucus in your stool, severe abdominal pain, vomiting for more than two to three days, or feeling like you need to poop but not actually producing anything when you go to the bathroom.

highlights.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
highlights.summary: As backlash grows over Flock's AI surveillance cameras, Texas Governor Greg Abbott has frozen state spending on them. The move came just ahead of the publication of a Texas Tribune investigation that revealed the state spent over $30 million on Flock cameras.
body: Flock cameras have increasingly drawn ire from across the political spectrum as they’ve become the subject of privacy concerns. There have been multiple incidents of officers being placed on leave or criminally charged for misusing Flock systems, including at least six in Texas alone. The company has also come under scrutiny for its data-sharing, the placement of some of its cameras near playgrounds, its own employees’ access to video feeds, unsecured video feeds, and its ham-fisted attempts to avoid transparency.

In recent months, cities around the country have been canceling their contracts with Flock, including many in Texas. Abbott’s Democratic opponent in the race for governor, Gina Hinojosa, has criticized him for expanding use of the cameras in the state. And Republican representative Keith Self recently posted on Instagram that, “From Flock cameras to kill switches, we will NOT surrender our Fourth Amendment rights to the growing surveillance state.” Cheering on the destruction of Flock cameras has even become a unifying pastime on the internet.

highlights.title: “We’re not doing 30 bets a year”: Vijay Pande on betting small after running $4 billion at a16z
highlights.summary: Vijay Pande — who left a16z's roughly $4 billion biotech practice last year to start the much smaller, AI-native VZVC — talks about why biology is finally shifting from a "discovery" science to an "engineering" one, why clinical trials are still brutally expensive, and why he thinks open, shared…
body: It used to be that Vijay Pande was better known in academic circles than investor circles. That changed pretty abruptly a dozen years ago, when Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz — who’d spent their firm’s first five years explicitly avoiding healthcare and life sciences — decided the category was worth betting on after all and handed the keys to Pande. At the time, he was a Stanford chemistry professor who was best known for building Folding@home, the distributed-computing project that turned millions of home PCs into a supercomputer for disease research. Over the next decade-plus, he grew a16z’s bet into a practice managing close to $4 billion.

So it was somewhat unexpected when in June of last year, Pande walked away from it all to start something much smaller. In fact, his new firm, VZVC, co-founded with longtime investor Zach Werner, is built around a handful of concentrated bets a year rather than dozens, it has no associates, and it relies heavily on AI for its day-to-day operations.

highlights.title: The kindness of strangers: My car had been towed and my kids had no shoes, then a man made a wonderful offer
highlights.summary: Can you help me?, I asked. I think my car’s been towed away, and my children don’t have any shoes. One of the first things we did after moving from the UK to Vancouver was buy a car. Unfortunately, I didn’t acquaint myself with the new road rules quite as quickly.
body: Which is to say, I didn’t know you aren’t allowed to park on busy streets after 3pm in Vancouver. Unaware and in a carefree summer mood, I parked outside an ice-cream shop and took my barefoot children in for a treat. We emerged a short time later, sticky and splattered in drops of raspberry, mint and chocolate, and found my car wasn’t there.

We were so fresh to Canada that we were still staying in a hotel. So I headed out on foot, one kid under each arm, towards our accommodation. When I reached the concierge desk of the valet parking place out the front, I frantically turned to the nicely dressed man standing there and launched into explaining our situation.
“Hi, can you help me? I think my car’s been towed away, and my children don’t have any shoes. I’m sorry about the ice-cream, but can you help me get to wherever the towing place is?”

He answered yes, of course, he was happy to help. After I badgered him about whether he’d have car seats for the kids, he said that we best get going, as he had to be back by 5pm. When I asked why, he replied, “Well, I’ve got a flight to catch.”

highlights.title: Big business has shown small firms what to do – and what not to do – with AI | Gene Marks
highlights.summary: Small business owners have watched large companies fumble – and sometimes succeed – with AI, and then use what works. One thing I’ve learned about corporate America is that what it succeeds at ultimately trickles down to benefit small businesses.
body: The good news is that it’s also the same for what they fail at.

This is the lesson so far with artificial intelligence. Thanks to the billions invested – and in many cases squandered – by big brands, SMBs (small and mid-sized businesses) have learned what works, what doesn’t, where to spend and where to abstain. Small businesses should be grateful. We’re getting the answers without paying for all the mistakes.

What works: AI for software development, customer service, security and voice. Big technology companies are already using AI to write, review and test code, allowing smaller development teams to accomplish more. Other firms have leaned in to AI to help with a variety of customer service processes with some success. IT departments are relying heavily on AI-enabled security platforms to detect and remedy unusual behavior, phishing attacks, and other vulnerabilities. Big brands are rolling out more AI-powered voice systems that answer incoming calls and perform rudimentary actions.
A countless number of the developers laid off by big tech are using AI tools to replicate themselves and provide services for smaller companies on a larger scale, and we’re hiring them.

highlights.title: Katseye’s Sophia to Sit Out European Leg of ‘Wildworld’ Tour to ‘Focus on Her Well-Being’
highlights.summary: Katseye member Sophia Laforteza will not be joining the group for the U.K. and European dates of their upcoming “Wildworld” tour, which is scheduled to launch on Tuesday.
body: This marks yet another wrinkle for Katseye, which has had a series of swings throughout the year. In February, just after they performed at the Grammys, member Manon Bannerman announced that she would be taking a temporary hiatus from Katseye to “focus on her health and wellbeing.” Earlier this month, Laforteza announced that she would be following suit so that she could prioritize her “mental health and wellness.” Then, just days before Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival, where they were slated to perform, the group dropped out of the lineup, citing member Megan Skiendiel’s ankle injury as the reason for their absence.

Amid it all, Katseye has continued to soar as a pop force, earning their first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 with “Wild” in August. The “Wildworld” tour is slated to kick off on Tuesday at Dublin’s 3Arena, with stops planned for Paris, Amsterdam and Copenhagen. Katseye will head back to the States for an extensive leg in North America beginning on October 13 at Miami’s Kaseya Center.

videos.summary: Build your Battle Deck and outsmart the enemy in fast real-time battles. From the creators of CLASH OF CLANS comes a real-time multiplayer battle game starring your favourite Clash characters and more. Start battling against players from around the world!
body: BECOME A MASTER OF STRATEGY AND DECK BUILDING
Choose unique Cards to your Battle Deck and head to the Arena for Battle!
Place your Cards right and knock down the enemy King and Tower Troops from their Towers in a strategic and fast-paced match.
points: Build your Battle Deck and outsmart the enemy in fast real-time battles.
From the creators of CLASH OF CLANS comes a real-time multiplayer battle game starring your favourite Clash characters and more.
Start battling against players from around the world!
Collect and upgrade 100+ Cards featuring the Clash of Clans troops, spells and defences you know and love and many others.
